extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, editorial staff and advisors submitting to or evaluating manuscripts for EMBO Press journals
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level editorial and ethical policies for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and publishing manuscripts in EMBO Press journals, including authorship, AI use, data and materials sharing, peer review models, reporting requirements, integrity checks, corrections, and transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (ICMJE-adapted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every author must meet ALL of the following criteria: Substantial contributions to the conception or design of the work; or the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data for the work; AND Drafting the work or revising it critically for important intellectual content; AND Final approval of the version to be published; AND Agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved. (adapted from the ICMJE authorship guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship implies that to the author’s best knowledge the text, schemata and data presented are original, cite relevant literature, and are accurate and reproducible. Violation may constitute scientific misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding authors must: ensure all listed authors have received and approved the manuscript before submission; relay all substantive correspondence with editors and reviewer reports to all listed authors; verify that new data/materials/code comply with transparency/reproducibility standards; agree to make all data underlying figures available as source data linked to the paper; confirm the paper accurately reflects original sources; conform to journal policies on sharing data/materials/code; and provide an institutional email address at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding authors also must ensure preservation and retrievability of original data/materials/code indefinitely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution declaration (CRediT mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of every author’s contribution must be specified using the Contributor Roles Taxonomy (CRediT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must be included in a mandatory author contribution section in every paper; free-text additional contributions may complement the CRediT entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI programs cannot be authors
rubrics_metrics.description: An Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Large Language Model (LLM) program cannot be listed as an author of an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship change and approval rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requires that all authors agree to the authorship as listed. Any changes in authorship or authorship order from the manuscript first submitted must be approved in writing to the journal’s editorial office by all of the original authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editors cannot decide or arbitrate on authorship matters and defer to appropriate institutional oversight structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-first and co-corresponding authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-first and co-corresponding authorship is permitted if multiple authors contributed equally and must be specified in the author list and detailed in the author contribution section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal discourages listing more than 5 co-first or co-corresponding authors; co-second or other co-authorship is not permitted. No explicit or implicit hierarchy for co-first or co-corresponding authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name-change policy after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who have changed their name may request updates to published papers; the journal will update the paper with the new name and redeliver updated metadata to indexing services without publishing a correction notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal public Author Correction is encouraged but silent corrections (no note on PDF/HTML) are permitted; authors should inform co-authors of the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use policy for manuscript preparation and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of AI programs should be primarily restricted to improve the style, accessibility or quality of human generated text and images. Any part of an article assembled with AI must be thoroughly checked and verified by the authors; authors bear full responsibility for factual accuracy, completeness, and citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose use in the published article, including details on which parts were assembled with AI and the tools employed. AI must not be used to synthesise or edit experimental data in a manner that misrepresents findings. AI-generated synthetic data must be clearly labeled in the main text and figure and documented in the Methods. AI can be used in collection/analysis if documented in Methods. Data figures and schemata must be original or accurately cite sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint posting encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: All EMBO Press Journals encourage posting primary research manuscripts on recognised community preprint servers (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv) before or in parallel with formal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts posted on bioRxiv/medRxiv will automatically forward-link to published EMBO Press papers. Declare preprint version in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: When formally citing a preprint: in-text: (preprint: NAME1 et al, YEAR); in reference list: Author NAME1, Author NAME2 (YEAR) article title. bioRxiv doi [PREPRINT].

rubrics_metrics.name: Scooping protection for preprints and during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Scooping protection applies from the day of posting a manuscript on a recognised preprint server in the same form as submitted, provided the manuscript is submitted to the journal within 4 months of posting. During editorial and peer review and the agreed revision period, other studies appearing in the literature are not taken into account in assessing conceptual advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform editors if you become aware of other directly relevant studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for reviewed preprints and Review Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press supports 'reviewed preprints'—preprints posted with public reviewer reports and author responses—and is affiliated with Review Commons; EMBO editors will assess manuscripts transferred from Review Commons based on existing reviewer reports without restarting review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may request posting of reviewer reports on the preprint; Review Commons peer review is a free community service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and reviewer anonymity options
rubrics_metrics.description: Default single-anonymous peer review: reviewers know author identities, reviewer reports provided to authors are anonymous. Authors may opt for double-anonymous review at initial submission; the responsibility to anonymise files lies with the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial offices will not edit files for anonymity and will not alert authors who fail to anonymise. The journal may consult reviewers after conditional acceptance on a de-anonymised manuscript to assess revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript technical checks and editorial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts undergo technical checks on submission and are assessed by a dedicated scientific editor specialised in the manuscript topics; editors may also consult Editorial Advisory Board members or external expert advisors before sending for formal peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research manuscripts judged potentially suitable with realistic experimental revision are sent for formal peer review; manuscripts with low probability of success can be returned without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and typical review panel size
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are typically reviewed by three appropriate independent experts selected by the editors. Authors may exclude a small number of experts due to conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EMBO Press reviewer guidelines for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making and revision invitation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on reviewers' arguments and recommendations, editors decide to offer publication, invite revision, or reject. Revisions are invited only for manuscripts that have a high probability of acceptance after one major round of experimental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions may involve consultation with reviewers, Editorial Advisory Board, and/or authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent process and publication of the Review Process File
rubrics_metrics.description: For accepted manuscripts, EMBO Press publishes as an online supplementary document (the Review Process File) all correspondence between authors and the editorial office relevant to the decision process, including all reviewer comments directed to the authors and authors' point-by-point responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal communications and informal consultations are excluded; reviewer anonymity is strictly maintained. Authors can opt out of the transparent process at any stage prior to publication. The author checklist will still be published even if authors opt-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Confidential Comments and transmission of reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press has removed the 'Confidential Comments' field from reviewer reporting forms so that authors receive all information pertinent to the decision. Reviewers should be aware that all comments will be transmitted to the authors and the other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers need to communicate confidentially about ethical standards, data integrity, biosecurity, or conflicts, they should contact the editorial office by email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer cross-commenting and reviewer identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are routinely invited to comment on each other’s reports and may discuss issues under moderation of the editors; reviewers are not informed of each other’s identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal experiments ethical approval and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For studies reporting experiments on live vertebrates and/or higher invertebrates, the corresponding author must confirm experiments were performed in accordance with relevant guidelines and include in Materials and Methods the institutional/licensing committee approving the experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may consult board members or external experts and reject manuscripts not conforming to NIH or MRC animal welfare guidelines. Authors are encouraged to follow the ARRIVE guidelines for reporting animal studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects ethics, consent, and clinical trial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For experiments involving human subjects, the corresponding author must identify the approving committee and include a statement that informed consent was obtained and that experiments conformed to the WMA Declaration of Helsinki and the Belmont Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors or reviewers may request documentation. Clinical trials should include a CONSORT flow diagram as supplementary information, follow CONSORT reporting guidelines, and be registered as recommended by ICMJE; retrospective registration is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines (EQUATOR recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to follow the EQUATOR Network reporting guidelines appropriate to study type (e.g., ARRIVE for animal research, CONSORT for randomised trials, PRISMA for systematic reviews, STROBE for observational studies, MIAME for microarray studies, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A table of recommended guidelines by study type is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosecurity and dual-use assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned research and results should be evaluated early for possible dual-use concerns; authors should consult an appropriate local body and explicitly describe potential biosecurity implications and the local body's assessment in the cover letter and author checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may balance risks and benefits of publication and consult board members/external experts in biosafety, biosecurity, or public and environmental health; ultimate decision rests with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity investigations and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal staff undertake routine image analysis and will request source data and author response to image aberrations. The journal will investigate suspected instances of scientific fraud, inappropriate image manipulation, plagiarism, misrepresentation, duplicate publication and other violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on outcomes, the journal may publish corrections, editorial expressions of concern, or retractions; institutions and employers may be informed. The journal will collaborate with institutional investigations and may accept their outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and plagiarism policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is misappropriation of intellectual property and substantial unattributed textual copying (including ideas, text, images, methods). Any information published should represent a substantial, novel contribution; overlapping submissions must be declared in the cover letter and included with submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal uses CrossCheck to screen for plagiarism (including self-plagiarism) prior to publication. The editors decide whether related text prevents publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integrity of images — screening and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal staff analyze image-based data before acceptance. Potential aberrations are classified according to a three-tiered system; editors may request source data and reserve the right to forego publication if key data do not meet integrity or reproducibility standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aberrations are noted the authors will be contacted and, depending on severity, the authors' institution may be contacted. See 'Classifying image aberrations' for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and reagents sharing expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: By publishing in an EMBO Press journal, authors agree to make available to colleagues all new reagents (organisms, viruses, cells, nucleic acids, antibodies, or means to produce them) used in the research that are not available from public repositories or commercial suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human patient samples/data must follow ethical standards. Materials must be made available at a reasonable cost that reflects production/distribution. Distribution does not confer co-authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and software availability expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets obtained by experimentation, computation or data mining should be made freely available without restriction, especially data central to the findings. Software should be described sufficiently (narrative, math, pseudocode, optionally source code) to allow reproduction; non-commercial users should be granted free access to implementations central to the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If third parties generated/analyzed part of the data, this must be stated in the data availability statement. Restrictions on availability/use must be clearly specified and may detract from impact and influence editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for review/publication: data deposition in public databases
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press will only review and publish manuscripts if authors agree to make all data that cannot be published in the journal itself (e.g., novel sequences, structural data, large-scale gene expression data) freely available, where possible, in appropriate public databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed data deposition guidance is provided under 'Data deposition.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition prior to submission and reviewer access
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale datasets, sequences, atomic coordinates and computational models should be deposited in relevant public databases prior to submission, provided private access is available at the database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enable reviewers to consider the data during peer review, include username and password details in the manuscript file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets and computer code generated in the study should be listed in a structured 'Data Availability' section placed after Methods. Each dataset should be a separate bullet including: 1) short description of measurement type, 2) repository name (or acronym), 3) DOI or accession number, and 4) a resolvable link (identifiers.org or full URL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit example format is provided. If the study includes no deposited data, state: 'This study includes no data deposited in external repositories'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished observations and personal communications policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not permit citation of 'Data not shown'. 'Unpublished observations' may be referred to only in exceptional cases and should list the persons in brackets. Personal communications must be authorised in writing by those involved, with authorisation sent at time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to manuscripts in preparation or submitted should be cited as '(Author name(s), in preparation)' and not included in references; copies should be enclosed at submission where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interest disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, reviewers, advisors, and editors are required to declare all potential or actual interests that could be perceived to influence presentation, interpretation, or assessment of an article at the earliest opportunity and before viewing or downloading relevant files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must include a declaration in the paper’s disclosure statement. Editors will exclude themselves from handling manuscripts owing to competing interests. View full competing interest policy with example statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal decisions if there is concrete evidence of a misunderstanding or mistake at the editorial or reviewer level by emailing the handling editor of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are evaluated in depth and without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer policy within and to EMBO Press
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have options to transfer manuscripts between EMBO Press journals; declined manuscripts include a link for transfer. Editors may confidentially consult with other EMBO journals about transfer; associated reviewer reports (and identities if agreed) and all files will be forwarded if the author initiates transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may opt out of transfer consultation when submitting. Transfer offers from select Nature Portfolio journals are optional; authors receive detailed requirements and a direct transfer link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting submissions with external reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press welcomes new submissions with reviewer comments from other journals. Authors should include a cover letter describing the situation and provide complete reviewer reports and a point-by-point response; editors will assess and may contact the original journal or reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may seek additional expert advice and discuss revision options prior to decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article corrections, errata, editorial notes, addenda and refutation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press will assess reported issues. Definitions: 'correction' = significant error by authors; 'erratum' = significant error by the journal; 'editorial note' = alert readers to a specific issue; 'addendum' = rare publication of additional data directly relevant to central aspects. Articles may be refuted in Correspondence with data; authors of refuted papers may be offered opportunity to respond; after one round of correspondence the matter is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For papers >=10 years old, clear evidence of data integrity issues affecting core claims is required to pursue a response. Image corrections follow the data integrity policy and may trigger institution contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and institutional notification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For serious scientific misconduct, the journal may ask authors to retract or impose retraction, and will inform authors' current employers and the research institution of the corresponding author at time of publication. The journal may publish an editorial expression of concern while matters are unresolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial notes can be updated as required. The journal collaborates with institutional investigations and may accept their outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author proof review obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are obliged to carefully review proofs. If an author finds a significant issue after online publication ahead of print, they should contact the journal immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher can usually make changes indicated by a footnote before issue assignment without a formal correction; changes after that stage will most likely require a formal correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Content of papers and associated press releases is strictly embargoed until the official date of publication. Accepted contributions can be discussed with media from one week before publication if journalists respect the embargo date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may arrange their own publicity but must adhere to embargo conditions; further details available from the editorial office.
